title: Auto-probe conductor for catalog and tenant pin transitions
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Goal: Build an automated 'probe conductor' service that launches a set of lightweight, budget-aware synthetic checks when a model version is pinned or a serving config changes (both catalog-wide promotions and tenant-specific pins). The conductor's responsibilities: 1) decide probe fanout and sampling based on tenant priority, traffic shape, and budget; 2) choose probe types (smoke/light/full fidelity) based on diff surface (model architecture change, quantization, KV cache behavior, prompt-format changes); 3) surface a single rollback score and a human-readable evidence bundle to the Console and to alerting channels; 4) integrate with existing eval harness and the preflight canary runner so results can gate automatic rollouts.

Context and motivation: Several recent incidents showed subtle regressions after pin/upgrade events where perf or hallucination rates drifted only for a subset of tenants or prompt patterns. We need a low-latency, automated early-warning pipeline that is tenant-aware and cost-bounded so we can flag risky promotions before full traffic cutovers or quickly roll back if signals are strong.

Key design decisions under consideration: - Sampling: mix deterministic tenant targeting (top-10 revenue/latency-sensitive customers) + stochastic traffic-weighted sampling to catch tail regressions. - Probe taxonomy: Smoke (liveness, canonical prompts, latency), Behavioral Light (top-10 tenant prompt families, sampling from recent logs), Full Fidelity (longer evals using tenant's eval set where available). - Budgeting: assign per-promotion budget and enforce token/compute caps; support an emergency fast-path that sacrifices sample breadth for speed. - Scoring: combine delta metrics (accuracy/fidelity, hallucination rate, latency P95, cost variance) with weights adjustable per tenant. Provide single 'rollbackScore' and suggested action (approve/hold/rollback). - Config diffs: trigger more aggressive probes when diffs include quantization changes, KV cache policy changes, kernel-level config, or sequence length profile shifts.

Non-goals: Full replacement of large-scale shadowing or customer-wide A/B tests. The conductor is intended as a preflight/early-detection system, not the final safety gate for every enterprise rollout.

Acceptance criteria (high level): - When a model pin event occurs, the conductor starts probes within 3 minutes for catalog pins and within 5 minutes for tenant pins (slower may be acceptable for low-priority tenants). - Probe orchestration respects per-event budget and stops when budget exhausted. - The Console shows per-pin probe status, aggregated rollbackScore, and links to raw probe outputs and representative examples. - If rollbackScore crosses configured thresholds, a gated action is emitted to the rollout service and a PagerDuty notification is created for SRE/Oncall. - Results are persisted to the eval store and usable by downstream regression dashboards.

Telemetry and observability: probe duration, tokens consumed, samples executed, per-metric deltas, rollbackScore distribution, and tenant-level affectedness. Dashboards: Pin-Probe Overview, Top failing tenants, Cost-by-probe-type.

Rollout plan: 1) Alpha with internal tenants and catalog dryness (Week 1-2) 2) Beta with opt-in customer tenants (Week 3-5) 3) Default-on for catalog pins with conservative thresholds (Week 6)

Potential risks and mitigations: - False positives leading to unnecessary rollbacks: mitigate by conservative thresholds, require human approval for high-impact tenants. - Cost overruns: enforce strict budgets, require a per-promotion budget param. - Privacy: ensure probes for tenant-specific evals run in tenant's data plane when required and scrub logs.
acceptance_criteria: Budget enforcement prevents >X tokens per promotion (configurable)
Console shows rollbackScore and link to evidence bundle
